verdicts.summary: Lean has a stronger form of it. Same inequality, same two directions, same quantifier, with an explicit constant in place of the paper's unnamed c: the Lean proves c = 1/6. The directions agree with (6.2): v_r = (1, -b_g) = (1, 1-√2) is radialSymbol and v_t = (b_g, 1) = (√2-1, 1) is timeSymbol, and TorusInverse.vector gives the same two vectors where the inverse operators use them. |n| is the Euclidean length (frequencyLength), as in the paper, and the hypothesis k ≠ 0 is the paper's n ∈ ℤ²∖{0}. The proof is the paper's: conjugate_product_lower bounds the algebraic norm below by 1 and radialConjugate_upper / timeConjugate_upper bound the conjugate above by 3·|n|_{ℓ¹} ≤ 6·|n|, which is the paper's 'conjugate has absolute value at most C|n|'.
